# Reading (locked before the Lean): eq_bdg4_XZ (first bound of (4.18))

Passage: manuscript/paper/sections/04-proof-wellposedness.tex lines 572, 579-586, 600-605, 611-612, 622.

Setting: section 2 standing setting (filtration = usual augmentation generated by W, N, F_0;
W a d-dimensional (F_t)-Brownian motion). Dimensions n, m, d >= 1, G in R^{m x n} (full rank is
in force but not used by this bound; a statement for every G is broader).

Hypotheses in force (see context): those of Lemma 4.3; the bound itself uses only
dX in S^2 (cadlag adapted R^n-valued, E sup_{t<=T} |dX_t|^2 < inf) and dZ in H^2_W (predictable
R^{m x d}, E int_0^T |dZ|_F^2 < inf). A statement for arbitrary such dX, dZ (no solution property,
no assumptions) is broader; printed claim = its instance dX = X^1 - X^2, dZ = Z^1 - Z^2 of Lemma
4.3 (in S^2 x H^2_W because Theta^1 - Theta^2 in the space S).

Constant: exists c0 > 0, forall c >= c0 (before all data, independent of T, n, m, d, G and the
processes).

Conclusion, for I_t = int_0^t < G dX_{s-}, dZ_s dW_s > = int_0^t (dZ_s^T G dX_{s-}) . dW_s:
 (a) I exists as a local Ito integral on [0, T] (continuous (F_t)-local martingale, I_0 = 0,
     the Ito integral of the predictable integrand dZ^T G dX_-);
 (b) E sup_{t<=T} |I_t| <= c ||G|| (E sup_{t<=T} |dX_t|^2)^{1/2} (E int_0^T |dZ_t|_F^2 dt)^{1/2},
     right side finite (line 600-605 and 611: "The four suprema ... are therefore integrable");
 (c) E[I_T - I_t] = 0 for every t in [0, T] (supremum criterion; the paper uses E I_T = 0).
||G|| = operator norm (a larger norm such as Frobenius would weaken the bound).

## Context of (4.18)
Context common to the (4.18) units: proof of Lemma 4.3 (lem:pert), Step 1,
manuscript/paper/sections/04-proof-wellposedness.tex lines 490-622. Hypotheses in force: Assumptions lip, G, mono
(ass:lip, ass:G, ass:mono) for (b, sigma, h, f, g) with constants L, G, alpha, beta_1, beta_2;
lambda in [lambda_lower, 1], lambda_lower in (0, 1]; Theta^1, Theta^2 solve the forced system
(4.1) at lambda with F_0-measurable initial data xi_0^k and forcings q^k (q^{b,k}, q^{sigma,k},
q^{f,k} progressively measurable square-integrable, q^{h,k} P (x) E-measurable square-integrable,
q^{g,k}_T in L^2(F_T)); X^k, Y^k cadlag adapted with E int (|X^k|^2 + |Y^k|^2) < inf,
X^k_T in L^2, Z^k in H^2_W, U^k in H^2_N, and Theta^1 - Theta^2 in the space S (so dX, dY in S^2,
dZ in H^2_W, dU in H^2_N). q denotes dq = q^1 - q^2. d sigma_t = sigma(t, Theta^1_t, mu^1_t) -
sigma(t, Theta^2_t, mu^2_t), d h_t evaluated at the predictable tuples (Theta^{k,-}_t,
mu^{k,-}_t) (L^2(nu; R^n)-valued, read through a P (x) E-measurable representative), mu^k_t the
Borel law flows of Lemma A.1. G in R^{m x n} full rank, ||G|| its operator norm.
The four bounds of (4.18) use only: dX, dY in S^2, dZ in H^2_W, dU in H^2_N, and the square
integrability of lambda d sigma + q^sigma and lambda d h + q^h (lines 606-610); the finiteness
claims of lines 600-610 use Assumption lip. The constant c_BDG is the universal one.

## Standing setting
Standing setting (manuscript section 2, manuscript/paper/sections/02-model-assumptions.tex lines 1-11): a filtered
probability space (Omega, F, (F_t), P) satisfying the usual conditions, horizon T > 0, dimensions
n, m, d >= 1, a d-dimensional (F_t)-Brownian motion W and an independent Poisson random measure N
on R_+ x E with intensity dt nu(de), nu sigma-finite on a countably generated (E, \mathcal E);
(F_t) is the usual augmentation of the filtration generated by W, N and an independent initial
sigma-field F_0. Ñ = N - dt nu. (2.1): E int int psi dN = E int int psi nu(de) ds in [0, inf] for
predictable psi >= 0. Spaces (section 3): S^2 = cadlag adapted with E sup_{t<=T} |V_t|^2 < inf;
H^2_W = predictable R^{m x d} with E int_0^T |Z|_F^2 < inf; H^2_N = predictable L^2(nu;R^m)-valued
with E int_0^T ||U||^2 < inf, read through a P (x) E-measurable representative ((2.8), Fubini
isometry). c_BDG (section 4, lines 22-37): one universal constant, valid for cadlag local
martingales, at p = 1 (Davis form, quadratic-variation form) and p = 2; it is fixed before all
data (C's depend on it). "Supremum criterion": a cadlag local martingale with integrable running
supremum has zero-mean increments.

# Comparison: eq_bdg4_XZ (Dissertation/PaperSpec/A/Sec4BDG.lean)

Setting: the paper's section-2 setting with the filtration enlJoint (as in the Lemma 4.1 units);
n, m, d > 0, T > 0.

Constant: "exists c0 > 0, forall c >= c0" outermost, before all data (independent of T, the
dimensions, G and the processes).

Hypotheses: JointBorel T C ((2.3)), Assumption23 (Lipschitz, constant L), G.rank = min m n
(Assumption 2.4, full rank), Assumption25 (monotonicity, alpha, beta_1, beta_2), 0 < lamLow <= lam
<= 1 (lamLow <= 1), xi_1, xi_2 F_0-measurable, two forcings of the paper's class (PredForcing: q^b,
q^sigma, q^f progressive, q^h marked predictable, square integrable, vanishing off [0, T], q^g_T
F_T-measurable in L^2), (X_k, Y_k, Z_k, U_k) solving (4.1) at lam in H_weak with X_T in L^2
(WeakForcedSolution), and supSize of the difference < inf (Theta^1 - Theta^2 in H). These are
exactly the hypotheses of Lemma 4.3 in force at (4.18). The bound itself uses only dX in S^2 and
dZ in H^2_W, but the proposition does not generalise: it states the printed point.

Conclusion: integrand (s, omega, j) |-> sum_k (G dX_{s-})_k dZ^{kj}_s = (dZ_s^T G dX_{s-})_j, i.e.
<G dX_{s-}, dZ_s dW_s>, with dX_{s-} the left limit of X_1 - X_2 for s in (0, T] and 0 elsewhere
(dZ vanishes off [0, T]). (a) exists M with IsLocalBrownianIntegral for enlJoint; (b) for every such
M: E sup_{t in [0,T]} |M_t| <= ofReal(c ||GX G||) (E sup |dX_t|^2)^{1/2} (sum_{k,j} energy
dZ^{kj})^{1/2} < inf, ||GX G|| being the operator norm of x |-> Gx between Euclidean spaces, i.e.
||G||; (c) E[M_T - M_t] = 0 with integrability for all t in [0, T]. Matches the first line of (4.18)
with its finiteness (lines 600-605, 611) and the supremum criterion (lines 611-612).

Witness: Dissertation.Acceptance.A.lem_pert_two_data_hypotheses
(Dissertation/Acceptance/A/WitnessSec4.lean): Example 5.1(i) with n = m = d = 1, nu = delta_0,
beta_1 = beta_2 = 1, sigma_c = h_c = 0, G = 1, lambda_lower = lambda = 1, zero forcings, initial
data 0 and e_1, and the solutions of Theorem 3.5. This is an instance the paper intends, and it
meets every hypothesis, so the proposition is not vacuous. But it does NOT exhibit nonzero
integrands: with deterministic initial data and no noise (sigma_c = h_c = 0, zero forcing) the
solutions are deterministic (X_t = Y_t = e^{-t} from e_1, Theta = 0 from 0, by uniqueness), so
dZ = 0, dU = 0, d sigma = -beta_1 dZ = 0, d h = -beta_1 dU = 0 and q = 0: all four integrands of
(4.18) and the fifth integrand vanish (dX and dY are nonzero). The hypotheses can be met with
nonzero integrands (e.g. different forcings q^{sigma,1} != q^{sigma,2} or q^{h,1} != q^{h,2}), but
no witness shows it.

Coverage paragraph:
Coverage (claim A:eq:bdg4, acceptance/claims.json; passage
manuscript/paper/sections/04-proof-wellposedness.tex lines 579-622). The five clauses state: the
four bounds of (4.18), each with the existence of its integral as a local stochastic integral (which
carries the local-martingale property), the finiteness of the bound and the zero mean of the
increments (the supremum criterion, lines 600-612); the finiteness of E int |lambda d sigma +
q^sigma|_F^2 and E int ||lambda d h + q^h||^2 (lines 606-610); and the L^1 bound of the fifth
integrand (lines 612-621). Two assertions of the passage are stated by no clause: the
predictability of the fifth integrand (lines 612-613, "The fifth has predictable integrand") and the
zero expectation of the fifth term by (2.2) (line 622, "Hence (2.2) applies, and all five terms have
zero expectation"). The scope note records the omission ("the compensated integral of an
integrable predictable integrand, not defined here") and reads the representative of
lambda d h + q^h as marked progressively measurable rather than predictable; but the same
inventory states the zero mean of M^2 in Lemma 4.1 in pathwise form (Poisson integral minus
compensator, lem41_M2_zero_mean), so the fifth term's zero mean could be stated the same way: as it
stands the claim's clauses do not state every assertion of its passage. The four zero means are
stated for every increment M_T - M_t, which at t = 0 (M_0 = 0) gives the printed zero expectation.
No clause states something the passage does not claim (the first links of the bounds, BDG at
p = 1, are cited and not stated; the end-to-end bounds have the printed right sides). The
hypotheses of every clause are exactly those of Lemma 4.3 in force at this point: Assumptions
2.3-2.5 with (2.3) joint Borel measurability, G of full rank, lambda in [lambda_lower, 1],
F_0-measurable initial data, forcings of the paper's class (q^h marked predictable), solutions of
(4.1) in H_weak with X_T in L^2, and Theta^1 - Theta^2 in H (supSize < inf); Assumption 2.2 is,
correctly, not assumed; no more, no fewer. The scope decision is still marked
scope_reviewed: false.

verdict.detail:
Representation choices, each harmless:
1. c_BDG read as "exists c0 > 0, forall c >= c0" (outermost, universal); the paper never fixes
   c_BDG's value.
2. Time axis R: Z, U and the forcings vanish off [0, T]; the left limits dX_{s-}, dY_{s-} are taken
   on (0, T] and set to 0 elsewhere (s = 0 is dt-null and N has a.s. no atom at time 0).
3. Expectations of nonnegative quantities are lintegrals in [0, inf] with the finiteness of the
   right side stated; |.|_F^2 and ||.||^2_{L^2(nu)} are coordinate sums of energies; ||G|| is the
   operator norm ||GX G|| of x |-> Gx between Euclidean spaces.
4. "Exists as a local stochastic integral" is IsLocalBrownianIntegral / IsLocalCompensatedIntegral
   for the paper's filtration enlJoint (reviewed in this chunk).
5. The solutions are those of WeakForcedSolution (H_weak with X_T in L^2), the difference in H
   through supSize < inf, the coefficient evaluations through the actual law Law(Theta_t) (and
   Law(Theta^-_t) for h) rather than the Borel representatives of Lemma A.1, which agree for a.e.
   t, so every integral and expectation is unchanged.

author_review.disagreements:
Agreement with the author's reading of the five propositions (setting, hypotheses exactly those of
Lemma 4.3, integrands, local-integral reading, bounds, finiteness, zero means, representatives of
lambda d h + q^h). Disagreements:
1. Witness. The review says lem_pert_two_data_hypotheses "does not exhibit nonzero integrands
   (... nothing is stated about dZ, dU or Sigma)". It is stronger than that: at this instance the
   integrands are zero. With sigma_c = h_c = 0, zero forcings and deterministic initial data 0 and
   e_1, the solutions are deterministic by uniqueness (Theta = 0 from 0; X_t = Y_t = e^{-t},
   Z = U = 0 from e_1), so dZ = 0, dU = 0, d sigma = -beta_1 dZ = 0, d h = -beta_1 dU = 0 and q = 0:
   all four integrands of (4.18) and the fifth integrand vanish a.e., and the witness exercises
   none of the integrals. The propositions are not vacuous (the hypotheses are met at an intended
   instance, and they can be met with nonzero integrands, e.g. with q^{sigma,1} != q^{sigma,2} or
   q^{h,1} != q^{h,2}), but no witness shows a nonzero instance.
2. Coverage. The review accepts the scope note's omission of "the fifth has predictable
   integrand" (lines 612-613) and of the zero mean of the fifth term by (2.2) (line 622) because
   they "need the fifth term itself, the compensated integral of an integrable predictable
   integrand". I do not think that justifies the gap: the predictability of the fifth integrand is
   a property of the integrand (a predictable representative of lambda d h + q^h paired with
   G^T dU), which needs no integral; and the same inventory states the zero mean of M^2 in Lemma
   4.1 pathwise (Poisson integral minus compensator, lem41_M2_zero_mean), so the fifth term's zero
   mean can be stated the same way. As it stands, the clauses of A:eq:bdg4 do not state every
   assertion of lines 579-622.
3. Representatives. The paper reads lambda d h + q^h through a P (x) E-measurable representative
   ((2.8)); the propositions quantify over marked progressively measurable ones. Harmless (the
   library integral depends only on the dP ds nu class and the paper's predictable representative
   is among them), but the review should say why, rather than only "as in eq_dX".
